note: Municipal baseline. invoice_date is deliberately NOT asserted: this renewal notice prints no issue date (only a due date and a page-footer print timestamp), so the value correctly defaults to today and would go red the next day. The generate twin answering with that footer timestamp is why invoice_date refuses an uncorroborated generate value. service_address and routingDecision are NOT asserted either: the address extract returns null on roughly 1 run in 3, and because service_address is base-critical that sends routing to review on those runs. Both billing-period dates are empty on all 10 runs, so the 1 is NOT derived from a period -- the analyzer invents a one-day period on a renewal notice that prints no service period. Recorded here rather than asserted, because a coin-flip assertion guarantees a future red run. payment_due_date 2025-12-31 is asserted from 2026-07-31, once the defaulting bug was fixed. This doc is the corpus's worst case for it: the printed date is read correctly on all 68 cached replicates, but its confidence sits low and noisy around the 0.73 bar (0.588 to 0.742 on 13 runs, 0.884+ on the rest), so nearly 1 run in 5 replaced a correct printed date with today+30 -- and because the due date is already in the PAST, the default masked an overdue renewal as not-yet-due. gates.evaluate now keeps a sub-threshold due date when the same calendar day is printed in the OCR text.
